notes: Breadboard naming: the image's row numbers 1-30 are the catalogue column; letters a-e are bank 't' and f-j are bank 'b'. The right-hand rail used as ground is written 'tp.<n>', with n the nearest row number; it is a single strip, so every hole on it is ground. The rail hole numbers are approximate.
Jumper 'a' is the Pi end (female socket on the header pin) and 'b' is the breadboard end (male). wire7 is male-to-male, with 'a' in 28t.d and 'b' in the ground rail.
Pi GND: the black wire goes to the GND pin beside GP3 (physical pin 6), which is GND.1 in the catalogue.

Each LED has its 330R resistor on the anode side, from the GPIO column across the centre gap to the LED anode. The LED cathode goes to the ground rail. The buzzer's + (pin 2) is on the GPIO15 strip and its - (pin 1) is on the ground rail.
Pushbutton: the row-28 legs (joined inside) go to ground and the row-30 legs go to GPIO21. The code does not use a pull-up resistor (GPIO Zero enables the internal pull-up).
GPIO signals are 3.3 V logic, with 330R resistors on every LED.
